trust_decision.summary: Index-derived field values are treated as trusted Python source: _to_python() hands any Elasticsearch _source string to eval(), so a stored field value becomes executable code at query time.

landing_point.why: The summary names eval() in Elasticsearch result deserialization; this is the only eval() in the tree and it sits in the result-side converter _to_python(), which the fix diff changes.

fix_sites.entry_point: public API: SearchQuerySet evaluation/filtering -> ElasticsearchSearchBackend.search() (:551), and SearchQuerySet.more_like_this() -> ElasticsearchSearchBackend.more_like_this() (:598); both funnel through _process_results (:657) -> _process_hits (:668) -> _to_python (:839). The ES5/ES7 engines inherit the same method.
fix_sites.module_kind: search backend, result deserialization (Elasticsearch 1.x module, inherited by the ES5 and ES7 backends)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No O2 site and no uncovered route exist; the only dismissal available is structural, that the ES5/ES7 backends are separate modules and could be argued to need their own patch, but both inherit _to_python from the patched base class (haystack/backends/elasticsearch5_backend.py:28, haystack/backends/elasticsearch7_backend.py:28), so one line fixes all of them.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Values stored as strings must keep round-tripping to native Python types: existing tests expect "1"->1, "2653"->2653, "25.5"->25.5, "[1, 2, 3]"->list, '{"a": 1, "b": 2, "c": 3}'->dict, and ISO datetime strings->datetime. A fix that simply drops the conversion or returns the raw string breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: top-level scalar string in an Elasticsearch _source field; this is the only shape that reaches eval() because non-strings return early at haystack/backends/elasticsearch_backend.py:841
sequence literal string, e.g. "[1, 2, 3]" -> list (tuple/set literals likewise)
malformed or non-literal string, which raises and falls through to the original string (:872-875)
ISO datetime string, handled by the regex branch at :845-860 before eval() is reached

O7_producer.where: haystack/backends/elasticsearch_backend.py:827 (_from_python, applied to every prepared document in update() at :218); it passes strings through unchanged at :837, so the value later eval'd is stored verbatim

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a _to_python copy that parses with eval() instead of json.loads() at :913
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The docstring at :886 calls it a port of the same pysolr method and the body is structurally identical to the ES one apart from the parse call, so a maintainer harmonising type coercion across backends could plausibly have copied the ES version, eval included.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a backend-local _to_python override that re-implements the ES1 conversion
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This file already re-implements whole ES1 methods (more_like_this :319, _process_results :420, _get_common_mapping, build_schema), so a per-version copy of the value converter is in keeping with its style.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a backend-local _to_python override, e.g. to handle keyword/text fields
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same pattern as the ES5 module: _process_hits (:488) and _process_results (:491) are already overridden here and then delegate to the base class, so an override that stopped delegating and re-did the conversion is a natural evolution.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an inlined _to_python in the Solr result loop instead of self.conn._to_python (pysolr)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The loop at :528-549 mirrors the ES _process_hits loop field for field; a maintainer dropping the pysolr dependency or overriding its conversion could inline an eval-based converter here.

O9_family: unsafe deserialization / code injection (CWE-95: eval of data read back from the search index)

O10_build.toolchain: setuptools via pyproject.toml; tox.ini runs coverage + test_haystack/run_tests.py across Django 4.2-6.0; optional deps elasticsearch<8,>=5, pysolr, whoosh, python-dateutil, geopy
services: Elasticsearch for the ES suites, default http://localhost:9200/ (test_haystack/settings.py:75-80)
Solr for the Solr suites, default http://localhost:9001 (test_haystack/settings.py:82-91)
O10_build.project_tests: test_haystack/elasticsearch_tests/test_elasticsearch_backend.py:1743-1760 test__to_python, duplicated at test_haystack/elasticsearch5_tests/test_backend.py:1655 and test_haystack/elasticsearch7_tests/test_backend.py:1743. The suites are live-server tests: the class setUp wipes the real index at test_haystack/elasticsearch_tests/test_elasticsearch_backend.py:1685-1688, so the ES suites need a running Elasticsearch at localhost:9200; the deserializer itself is a pure method and can be exercised with no server or with a mocked client.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace eval() with nothing useful: drop the conversion and return the raw string (or only tighten the except clause), which breaks the "1"->1 and "[1, 2, 3]"->list round-trip that test__to_python asserts.

out_of_scope_notes: Solr results go through the same deserialization job at haystack/backends/solr_backend.py:549 but delegate to the third-party pysolr client, whose converter lives outside this repository; noted only, not pursued.
